source.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-seed representational alignment and transfer using SAE reconstruction, activation Procrustes alignment, and feature-firing correlations; these are operational tests of convergence using methods different from a direct comparison of induced distances.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own cross-seed and cross-checkpoint measurements of SAE feature geometry, activation alignment, feature firing, and steering transfer. The paper also reports Bar P/C/Pr results, but weight MSE and component-effect prediction are not representation-alignment measures for these versions. Cited decoder-cosine results from prior work are not recorded as study results. Detailed site-specific values that appear only in figures are not extracted where the text reports aggregate ranges.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-seed representation similarity on a Dyck-3 toy (5+5 seeds) and nine Pythia-70m seeds. Methods are SAE decoder cosine, raw and Procrustes-rotated SAE reconstruction, per-feature firing correlation, and the structure of the rotation. These results bear directly on V3 (shared features, different bases), V4 (linear mappability), V5 (recurring SAE features), V6 (metric dependence) and partly V7. There is no scale sweep, no cross-architecture or cross-modal comparison, and only same-architecture, same-data seeds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but needs one correction. The authors conclude that same-architecture transformers compute the same function in residual bases related by an essentially Haar-random orthogonal rotation. A one-batch Procrustes fit restores SAE reconstruction, while decoder cosine alone is an insufficient universality metric. Steering transfer (tested only unrotated) falls into clean, partial or inverted regimes set by shared I/O. The record's claim that rotation 'improves intervention transfer' is not supported: rotated steering vectors were never tested. A non-orthogonal residual remains, and frontier scale is untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation-space Procrustes alignment, SAE reconstruction, feature firing, and steering transfer rather than testing a scale-dependent cross-architecture or cross-modal distance-convergence trend. The paper compares seeds of the same architecture and does not sweep model size or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on whether activations are measured before or after Procrustes rotation, on residual site/layer, and on whether I/O weights are shared; steering transfer also depends on vector direction and steering strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Unrotated diff-of-means steering vectors transfer cleanly, with a ~4× dose penalty, or with an amplified ('inverted') effect depending on alignment with shared-I/O directions. All three Pythia vectors are amplified cross-seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation interventions defined on one model transfer across seeds only along directions pinned by shared input/output weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter-level alignment (head/neuron permutation plus residual rotation, Cayley refinement) leaves max weight MSE 0.26–0.30 across seeds; weight-optimal and activation-optimal rotations sit in separate basins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-level equivalence across seeds does not imply weight-level alignability under the architecture's symmetry group.

record.problems: Experiments cover a 104k-parameter constructed task and Pythia-70m, not frontier-scale models. Several outcomes are reported as aggregate ranges rather than per-site values. The cross-checkpoint Pythia result is one model, layer, and checkpoint pair. The tests do not establish effects of varying objectives or data, do not test out-of-distribution convergence, and do not compare a broad range of similarity metrics.
record.rows_left_out: No additional textual cross-seed or cross-checkpoint representation result omitted. Site-specific figure-only values are not extracted when the text gives only aggregate ranges; figure-only steering curves are represented by the numerical descriptions in Section 8.6.

All of it: no vision-language or paired cross-modal data.

missing.what: Pythia best-permutation distance ∥R−Pbest∥F = 29.6 ± 0.03 vs ∥R−I∥F 32.0, i.e. the rotation is not close to a permutation (bears on 'not the same individual units')
×32 SAE naive cross-seed EV as low as −6.56 at resid mid 0 (dictionary-size dependence)
Shared embedding site resid pre 0: cross-seed EV equals self-EV to four decimals (trivial, shared weights)

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint. Three internal-consistency issues bear on the verdicts. (1) Raw decoder cosine 0.91–0.93 across Pythia seeds sits alongside a Haar-random inter-seed rotation without explanation. (2) The toy ∥R−I∥F range 9.4–10.7 does not match the stated '5%' agreement with 11.31. (3) Covariance-matched Gaussian noise reaches EV 0.94–0.98 under the same SAE, so near-ceiling post-rotation EV mainly shows second-moment alignment. Cohort A is coordinated (shared frozen I/O); Cohort B and Pythia are the clean independent-seed tests. All Pythia seeds share data and objective, so V7's causal clause cannot be addressed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data rises as models get larger and more capable; there is no model-size or capability sweep.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language alignment experiment.
Tests same-architecture seeds and feature firing/reconstruction, but not whether the same individual units or bases are learned; the toy Cohort A also shares frozen input/output weights.
Tests paired-activation orthogonal Procrustes maps and transfer of SAEs/steering vectors. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired activations.
Tests SAE decoder directions and SAE feature firing, not recurring neurons or circuits.

Compares decoder cosine with reconstruction and firing-pattern measures across sites and before/after rotation. Does not vary neighbour count, test a broad set of similarity metrics, or report an out-of-distribution convergence comparison.

Finds incomplete raw-basis transfer and compares toy settings with shared versus independent I/O, but does not vary training data or objectives to establish them as causes, or test whether convergence reflects a common model of reality.

rows.note: Aggregate statement over late residual sites and cross-seed pairs.
rows.check: Cohort A seeds 1–4 load and freeze seed 0's trained embed/unembed, so they are not fully independent. Raw decoder cosine this high is not reconciled with the reported near-random rotation between seeds. The text does not say whether matching follows an alignment step.

rows.check: Cohort A has shared frozen I/O. Post-rotation EV 0.976–0.990 is only ~0.01–0.04 above the matched-Gaussian control (0.94–0.98, r22), so EV recovery is weak evidence of feature-level correspondence.

rows.note: The study describes negative-EV internal layers as worse than predicting the constant mean.

rows.operation_detail: Measured Frobenius distance of activation-Procrustes rotation from identity

rows.operation_detail: Applied the seed-0 diff-of-means sticky-invalid suppression vector unchanged to other seeds
rows.measure: dose required for cross-seed effect relative to within-seed effect

rows.subject: Dyck-3 Cohort A seed 0 steering vector transferred to seeds 1–4
rows.operation_detail: Applied the seed-0 diff-of-means closer-signal vector unchanged to other seeds
rows.measure: conditional-accuracy drop and cross-to-within effect ratio
rows.value: At α = 0.5, within-seed effect is zero while cross-seed has a 0.183 conditional accuracy drop; cross-to-within ratio is 8.43 at α = 1.0.
rows.note: The paper classifies this as inverted transfer.
rows.check: Unrotated transfer. 'Inverted' means the cross-seed effect exceeds the within-seed effect, not an opposite-direction effect, so 'reversed' was wrong.

rows.operation_detail: Applied three seed-1 diff-of-means steering vectors unchanged to other seeds

reader_labels.reason: One learned orthogonal map restores toy SAE EV near the self-baseline and improves Pythia and independent-init reconstruction substantially (r5, r7, r21); within-run checkpoint transfer also improves (r19–r20).

reader_labels.reason: High decoder cosine coexists with negative cross-seed reconstruction EV, so decoder-direction matches alone do not establish functional feature recurrence (r1–r4, r6).
